text:
alex: Seeing intermittent gRPC streams to model-serving pods stall across us-east-1 GPU fleet. GPU work queues freeze for 10-30s, then resume. No OOMs, CPU low. Logs show repeated 'stream reset' and long pauses.

infra-bot: alert: grpc_stream_errors > 5% (last 5m) on service/model-serving-us-east-1, triggered by 1770023345.

maya: I pulled tcpdump on one affected pod -> lots of IP fragments and duplicated ACKs. Looks like fragmentation + retransmits.

samir: Are we using an overlay? What's node MTU vs pod veth MTU? send `ip link` and `ip -d link` outputs from a bad node pls.

alex: pasted sample from node-a:```
$ ip link show ens5
2: ens5: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
$ ip link show vxlan.calico
45: vxlan.calico: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default
$ ip -s link show vethabc123
4: vethabc123: mtu 1440 qdisc noqueue state UP mode DEFAULT group default
IP fragment info from tcpdump:
16:23:02.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 12345, frag 1/2) 10.0.2.1 > 10.0.3.4: IP fragment 1/2
```

lina: This rings a bell — our RDMA/SR-IOV GPU nodes have NIC MTU 9000 for RoCEv2, but the overlay (vxlan/calico) is 1500 and some veths show 1440. Encapsulation overhead + wrong CNI MTU cause fragmentation when traffic crosses from SR-IOV nodes to non-SR-IOV nodes. RoCE encapsulated packets get chopped.

maya: Could be a PMTU blackhole too. Try `ping -M do -s 8000 <peer>` across nodes to confirm. Also `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` as an interim mitigation.

ops-oncall: Quick mitigation options: 1) set CNI mtu to 8950 for SR-IOV node pool (gives headroom for vxlan/encap) and restart calico/node only on that nodepool; or 2) disable GSO/TCP segmentation offload on affected veths as a stopgap (loss in perf). Can't change full cluster MTU without rolling impact.

samir: I'll prepare a daemonset that enforces iface MTU on the GPU node pool and a calico config patch for mtu per-nodepool. Will test in staging (staging-gpu-1) first. Also checking encapsulation type (ipip vs vxlan) because overhead differs.

alex: also adding an alert for prolonged gRPC stream stall (>=30s) to catch regressions. Assigning: samir -> patch + staging test, maya -> run ping+tcpdump checks, lina -> confirm SR-IOV nodes list and NIC config, ops-oncall -> approve rollout window. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: noted. will schedule maintenance window for rolling restart if needed.

maya: one more note — if we go mtu-for-nodepool route, update the Redwood-serving runtime to advertise smaller chunk sizes or enable chunk-level retries to smooth transient stalls.

alex: thanks. keep updates in this thread.
